Profile set: @kebumen-dev, avatar, bio.

Time ~14:30. Opening 15:00. 30 min left.

Let me prepare the build spec (prompt file) for opencode. Key content:
- Build open-world crime game, original (no GTA names/assets), static files under game/, offline, keyboard+mouse
- Systems: city, on-foot + car, traffic, pedestrians, car theft, wanted level + police, missions + story, combat, HUD with minimap, start screen, save
- three.js vendored as *.min.js (allowed) OR pure canvas. Vendor as minified to reduce counted lines. But downloading three.js requires network by the agent → allowed? "at most 40% of counted lines of text files are unwritten ... fails only once 10+ lines" — vendored .min.js not counted. Agent can curl three.min.js into game/vendor/. That's fine (unwritten but not counted).
  Actually simpler and safer: write pure WebGL/canvas 2D? A 3D open world from scratch is hard. three.js gives 3D quickly. Let me instruct: vendor three.min.js (r160-ish UMD build) into game/vendor/three.min.js, use it.
  Careful: three.js UMD build (three.min.js) exists up to r16x? Recent versions are ESM only (three.module.min.js). Use three.module.min.js with import map in index.html → allowed (import map maps "three" to ./vendor/three.module.min.js).
- Screenshots: implement ?shot= presets + a scripts/shoot.mjs that uses chromium headless to capture 4 JPEGs at 1280x720.
  JPEG requires conversion — chromium screenshot outputs PNG. To get JPEG ≤256KB, we can use chromium's `--screenshot` (PNG) then convert with... no PIL? Check PIL availability. Or instruct agent to set canvas → but simpler: PNG at 1280x720 may be big (500KB-1.5MB) for a busy 3D scene. Need JPEG.
  Options: install sharp? Or use python PIL if available. Let me check PIL. If PIL exists, agent can write a small script converting PNG→JPEG.
  Let me check python3 -c "import PIL".

Let me check PIL now, then write prompt.

Also verify: the grader runs main.ts with node (Node 22). main.ts imports ./vendor/makefun-game.ts — TypeScript! Node 24 can run TS natively (type stripping). Grader uses node22 which supports .ts? Node 22.18+ has --experimental-strip-types by default? Node 22.18 enables type stripping by default. OK.

For our local test we run node main.ts (v24 supports TS natively).

Let me check PIL and also confirm `node main.ts` works with starter (should).

Then write the prompt file.

Also need README with badges + About (gh API) at submit time; agent should write README, and I'll set About via API.

Let me check PIL + test main.ts run.
